reason: Grouping fibres seems like a useful first step toward building a muscle that can move the arm.
expectation: I expect a bundle or group of muscle fibres, though it may still need connective tissue.

alternatives.reason: Adding blood vessels also seems useful, but I want to build the muscle first.

effect: The fibre bundle is ready to be organized further with connective tissue.
reaction: The paired poses help connect the individual fibre's shortening to the bundle.
reason: Adding sheaths looks like the next step toward building a muscle.
expectation: I expect a wrapped muscle bundle or a more complete muscle.

alternatives.reason: Blood vessels will also help build the arm, but I want to continue assembling the muscle first.

effect: The sheaths form tendons that carry the biceps' pull, and the muscle cannot push the bone back; I still need to connect the opposing muscles.
reaction: The link from sheaths to tendons makes the construction clearer.
reason: Adding blood vessels is the only offered combination and should advance the arm assembly.
expectation: I expect an arm skeleton supplied with blood vessels, though I am unsure how that will enable the muscle attachment.

effect: Adding blood vessels produced an arm assembly with slots for opposing muscles, so I can now attach them.
reaction: The attachment points clarify what the assembly needs, though the blood vessels' role in creating it is not explained.
reason: The biceps is ready, and its shortening was shown bending the elbow, so I will fit it first.
expectation: I expect the biceps to fill the flexor slot, leaving the extensor slot open.

alternatives.reason: The triceps should fill the opposing slot, but either attachment seems like a reasonable first step.

effect: The biceps is fitted, leaving the triceps as the next attachment for the opposing muscles.
reaction: The fitting followed my expectation; nothing else notable changed.
reason: The triceps is the only offered combination and should complete the opposing pair.
expectation: I expect the triceps to fill the extensor slot, producing an arm with opposing muscles.

effect: The opposing muscles are fitted, and coordinated activation and relaxation explain how the forearm can bend and straighten.
reaction: The explanation makes the purpose of the opposing pair clear.
reason: Adding the shoulder and hand tissues is the only offered combination and should advance the arm assembly.
expectation: I expect a more complete arm with its shoulder and hand supported, though I am unsure whether this completes the goal.

effect: Adding the shoulder and hand tissues produced a supplied moving arm and completed the goal.
reaction: The completed arm brings the pieces together, though the final result adds little explanation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the biceps with tendons was most worthwhile: the explanation connected the fibre bundle and sheaths to a pull on the bone, and clarified why an opposing muscle is needed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the shoulder and hand tissues felt least informative: it completed the arm, but their contribution was only shown in outline.

surprise.text: I was surprised that adding blood vessels produced the assembly with muscle attachment slots; the result did not explain that connection.

arbitrary.text: The blood-vessel combination felt somewhat arbitrary as the step that made muscle attachment possible, even though supplying the arm with blood is a plausible part of the larger construction.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in continuing to see how the moving arm connects to other body systems. The explanations of tendons and opposing muscles were useful, though several later choices were simply the only available action.
